import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "The QKV Framework: The Library Analogy"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Every word generates three vectors: Query, Key, and Value.",
            "The Query represents what the word is looking for.",
            "Keys act like labels on a library's bookshelves.",
            "Values contain the actual information to be retrieved.",
            "Matching Queries to Keys identifies the relevant information."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        QUERY_COLOR = "#00FF00"
        KEY_COLOR = "#3366FF"
        VALUE_COLOR = "#FFCC00"
        HIGHLIGHT_COLOR = "#FFFF00"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # A search box labeled 'Query' (#00FF00) appears. Color L1 to #FFFF00.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        
        query_box = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.1, height=0.6, width=1.5, color=QUERY_COLOR)
        query_text = Text("Query", font_size=18, color=QUERY_COLOR)
        query_group = VGroup(query_box, query_text)
        
        # [Issue 31 Fix]: query_group at B4 to avoid crowding against title
        self.place_at_grid(query_group, 'B4', scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(query_group))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Multiple book icons labeled 'Key' (#3366FF) appear. Color L2 to #FFFF00.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        
        keys_group = VGroup()
        for i in range(3):
            # Book representation
            book_rect = Rectangle(height=0.8, width=0.6, color=KEY_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.3)
            book_spine = Line(book_rect.get_corner(UL), book_rect.get_corner(DL), color=KEY_COLOR, stroke_width=4)
            key_label = Text(f"Key {i+1}", font_size=14, color=KEY_COLOR).next_to(book_rect, DOWN, buff=0.1)
            keys_group.add(VGroup(book_rect, book_spine, key_label))
        
        keys_group.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.4)
        
        # [Issue 32 Fix]: Use place_in_area to center keys relative to query box
        self.place_in_area(keys_group, 'C3', 'C5', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(Create(keys_group))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # The 'Value' (#FFCC00) content inside the books is shown. Color L3 to #FFFF00.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        
        values_group = VGroup()
        for i in range(3):
            val_content = Rectangle(height=0.4, width=0.4, color=VALUE_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.6)
            val_text = Text(f"V{i+1}", font_size=12, color=WHITE).move_to(val_content)
            val_item = VGroup(val_content, val_text)
            # Position values initially inside books
            val_item.move_to(keys_group[i][0].get_center())
            values_group.add(val_item)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(values_group))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # The 'Query' matches with the correct 'Key' book. Color L4 to #FFFF00.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        
        # Matching Query to Key 2
        target_key = keys_group[1]
        matching_ray = Line(query_group.get_bottom(), target_key.get_top(), color=HIGHLIGHT_COLOR, stroke_width=2)
        
        self.play(Create(matching_ray))
        self.play(
            target_key.animate.set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR).scale(1.1),
            query_group.animate.set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # The matched book opens, highlighting its 'Value'. Color L5 to #FFFF00.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        
        target_value = values_group[1]
        others = VGroup(
            keys_group[0], keys_group[2], 
            values_group[0], values_group[2], 
            matching_ray
        )
        
        # Create an isolated pair for the final result
        q_copy = query_group.copy()
        k_copy = target_key.copy()
        v_copy = target_value.copy()
        isolated_pair_group = VGroup(q_copy, k_copy, v_copy).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.5)
        
        # [Issue 33 Fix]: Position isolated pair in area B4-D4 to avoid bottom edge crowding
        self.place_in_area(isolated_pair_group, 'B4', 'D4', scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(others),
            FadeOut(query_group),
            FadeOut(target_key),
            FadeOut(target_value),
            FadeIn(isolated_pair_group)
        )
        
        # Highlighting the "Retrieved" value

            isolated_pair_group[2].animate.scale(1.3).set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR),
            Write(retrieved_text)
        )
        self.play(Flash(isolated_pair_group[2], color=HIGHLIGHT_COLOR))
        
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Spotlight of AI: Understanding the Attention Mechanism in Transformers
outline.target_audience: University students and aspiring AI developers

sections.title: The Problem: The Memory Fog
sections.content: Introduce the limitation of older models (RNNs) that process words one by one. Explain how they 'forget' the beginning of a long sentence by the time they reach the end. This establishes the 'Why' for the Attention Mechanism.
sections.example: Imagine a goldfish trying to read a 100-page novel; by page 10, it has already forgotten the character's name introduced on page 1.

sections.title: Prerequisite: Words as Coordinates
sections.content: Explain Word Embeddings. Before 'Attention' happens, words must be converted into vectors (lists of numbers) in a multi-dimensional space where similar meanings are physically closer to each other.
sections.example: In a 3D plot, the words 'King' and 'Queen' are neighbors, while 'Toaster' is miles away in a different corner of the graph.

sections.title: The Core Concept: Dynamic Weighting
sections.content: Introduce the idea that not all words in a sentence are equally important to a specific word. Define 'Attention' as a mathematical way to assign a 'weight' or 'relevance score' between words.
sections.example: In the sentence 'The animal didn't cross the street because **it** was too tired,' the word 'it' shines a bright spotlight on 'animal' and a dim light on 'street'.

sections.title: The QKV Framework: The Library Analogy
sections.content: Break down the mathematical trinity: Query (Q), Key (K), and Value (V). Use a visual search analogy to explain how the model 'retrieves' information.
sections.example: Query (Q): Your search term in Google. Key (K): The titles of the search results. Value (V): The actual content of the webpage you decide to read.

sections.title: The Math: From Dot Product to Softmax
sections.content: Visualize the calculation: (Q × K) determines similarity (Dot Product). Use a Softmax function to turn these scores into percentages (0 to 1) that sum to 100%. This creates a 'Probability Map' of focus.
sections.example: An animated bar chart where 'Apple' (Query) hits 'Fruit' (Key) and gets a 0.9 score, but hits 'Computer' (Key) and gets 0.1. The higher the bar, the more information is pulled from that Value.

sections.title: Multi-Head Attention: Parallel Perspectives
sections.content: Explain that the model doesn't just look once; it looks multiple times simultaneously. This allows the model to understand different relationships (grammar, logic, emotion) at the same time.
sections.example: Imagine a detective team investigating a crime scene: one 'head' looks for fingerprints (grammar), another looks for a motive (context), and a third looks at the clock (tense).

sections.title: Application: Why LLMs Feel Human
sections.content: Conclude by showing how this mechanism allows Large Language Models like GPT-4 to maintain perfect context over thousands of words, enabling them to write coherent stories or code.
sections.example: A visual flow showing a prompt about a 'Space Cat' being transformed through layers of attention until the model generates a perfect description of a feline astronaut.

The Query represents what the word is looking for.
Keys act like labels on a library's bookshelves.
Values contain the actual information to be retrieved.
Matching Queries to Keys identifies the relevant information.
animations: A search box labeled 'Query' (#00FF00) appears. Color L1 to #FFFF00.
Multiple book icons labeled 'Key' (#3366FF) appear. Color L2 to #FFFF00.
The 'Value' (#FFCC00) content inside the books is shown. Color L3 to #FFFF00.
The 'Query' matches with the correct 'Key' book. Color L4 to #FFFF00.
The matched book opens, highlighting its 'Value'. Color L5 to #FFFF00.

storyboard.title: The Math: From Dot Product to Softmax
lecture_lines: Dot products calculate the similarity between Queries and Keys.
These raw scores indicate how well words match.
Softmax turns scores into percentages that sum to one.
This creates a clear probability map of focus.
The model pulls information based on these weights.
animations: Formula 'Q · K = Similarity' appears on screen. Color L1 to #FFFF00.
An arrow points from the formula to a result score. Color L2 to #FFFF00.
A 'Softmax' bar chart turns scores into percentages. Color L3 to #FFFF00.
A large data block flows from high-percentage 'Value'. Color L4 to #FFFF00.
A probability map (#00FFFF) overlays the word sequence. Color L5 to #FFFF00.

storyboard.title: Multi-Head Attention: Parallel Perspectives
lecture_lines: Transformers use multiple heads to process data simultaneously.
Each head focuses on a different type of relationship.
Different heads track grammar, logic, or tone.
animations: A central word is surrounded by three 'Heads' [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/head.svg] (#FF0000, #00FF00, #0000FF). Color L1 to #FFFF00.
Each head [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/head.svg] scans the word with a different colored ray. Color L2 to #FFFF00.
Labels 'Grammar', 'Logic', 'Tone' appear next to rays. Color L3 to #FFFF00.

storyboard.title: Application: Why LLMs Feel Human
lecture_lines: Attention allows models to maintain context over long texts.
This enables coherent storytelling and complex code generation.
It's the engine behind the intelligence of modern AI.
